Another enhancement relative to the state-of-the-art LDA process is that this proposed process improves the sourcing of synonym pools. For this work, salient words we extracted from each corpus individually, and are then added into a collective synonym pool. Since there was a large amount of overlap in salient topics between the two corpora, this was deemed to be appropriate, and resulted in a shared synonym pool. Any differences in topic saliency are therefore attributable to the results of the LDA process, not to differences in the pool of synonyms from which LDA can select. Synonym mapping randomization activity diagram BERTopic Implementation As seen on the left side of Figure 33, the present work integrates BERTopic results as an evenly weighted contribution to the START metric. After splitting each corpus into a list of sentences, the list is used to fit a BERTopic model. The models are then queried for each of the 10 categories. A keyword query returns the 𝑛 topics that have the highest similarity to the keyword, and the terms with the highest c-TF-IDF scores within those topics. The BERTopic function find_topics(search_term) generates an embedding for the search term and compares this embedding to the previously generated topics to determine similarity. From these top topics (𝑛 = 3), the scores of relevant words are summed to arrive at a category c-TF-IDF score. During this step we observed that BERTopic had a higher recall for relevant words given a search term than did LDA. For example, “rebate” scored highly in topics closely related to the “policy/incentives” BERTopic query, whereas “rebate” was not identified as a salient term according to LDA. 1.1. Score of Topic and Related Terms This project proposes to use the Score of Topic and Related Terms (START) as a metric for achieving a comprehensive ranking for a pre-determined category in a body of texts. The START metric takes an equal weighting of a category’s saliency and c-TF-IDF and represents the importance of the category as a single value, as shown in Figure 35. 84 Bradley, T.H., et al., Agent-Based, Bottom-Up Medium- and Heavy-duty Electric Vehicle Economics, Operation, Charging and Adoption, Final Technical Report, DE-EE0009664 Figure 35.
